lines: Worsening cough and fever over the past 4 days after being found unconscious at home following a 3-day drinking binge.

This 57-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, and a history of recurrent aspiration pneumonia including a prior lung abscess in July 2022, presents with worsening cough and fever over the past 4 days after recently being found unconscious at home following a 3-day binge.
He is brought to the emergency department by his partner.
He reports that over the past several weeks he has had multiple episodes of vomiting and poor oral intake.
He now reports producing foul-smelling brown sputum and experiencing right-sided chest discomfort.

encounters.cc: Brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision with significant hemorrhage requiring massive transfusion.

lines: Brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision with significant hemorrhage requiring massive transfusion.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, and nonvalvular atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin therapy who presents following a motor vehicle collision, with prior encounters significant for atraumatic splenic rupture and Mallory-Weiss tear.
He is immediately taken to the operating room for exploratory laparotomy and requires a massive transfusion protocol due to significant hemorrhage.
During the procedure, the patient develops perioral numbness and carpopedal spasm.
